title: decentralized-slab-autoscaler-with-commitment-reconciliation
author: Priya Desai
description: Context: Dedicated fleet tail latency and cost efficiency are sensitive to coarse-grained autoscaling signals and centralized decision bottlenecks. Motivation: introduce a decentralized slab-based autoscaler that reconciles tenant commitments with local pod-level signals to reduce orchestration churn while preserving throughput guarantees. Summary: this PR implements a decentralized slab autoscaling algorithm and a lightweight commitment reconciliation layer. Key ideas: 1) Slabs: time-bounded capacity slabs (e.g., 30s windows) are advertised cluster-wide with soft guarantees; nodes independently accept slab allocations based on local occupancy and heuristic headroom; 2) Commitment reconciliation: a background reconciler streams commitment deltas (commit, revoke) from the control plane and uses an idempotent, monotonic ledger to converge state without centralized locks; 3) Safety fences: local conservative allocator prevents oversubscription by reserving a minimal safety margin, with a burst-fallback path that uses short-lived soft credits; 4) Telemetry and observability: per-slab util histograms, convergence lag gauges, and commit delta counters are emitted; 5) Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag slab_autoscaler_v1, canary to 5% of clusters, experiments to compare per-tenant tail latency. Design notes: the reconciler uses vector-timestamped deltas and tombstones to achieve eventual consistency; node-level allocation prefers minimizing slab fragmentation to improve batching efficiency; slabs expire with lease-driven TTL and are auto-refreshed by nodes that serve as slab-anchors. Backwards compatibility: legacy reservation endpoints remain supported; the reconciler will only activate when the feature flag is set. Tests and results: unit tests for ledger convergence, integration tests with simulated 10k-tenant workloads, and a perf bench showing a 7.8% reduction in mean cost-per-token under bursty traffic and a 12% reduction in tail-latency violations in the canary run. Migration: a migration job converts legacy reservations to slab commitments in-place under the control plane; a fallback toggle allows rolling back instantly. This description includes implementation rationale, configuration knobs (slab_window_sec, safety_margin_pct, anchor_selector), testing summary, and rollout strategy.

Priya Desai: Reply: added detailed comments in monotonic_ledger.go and implemented tombstone vector timestamps to ensure idempotency. The reconciler tolerates transient partitions; leases and TTLs bound misallocation windows.
Anika Rao: Please add more unit tests for a double-apply scenario where deltas arrive out of order. Also add an e2e canary check for slab expiry behavior.
Priya Desai: Added tests (slab_simulator_test.go) and an e2e check in the canary harness. Fixed an ordering bug which caused a 10% over-reservation in a synthetic partition test.
Marcus Chen: LGTm pending CI. Recommend limiting default slab_window_sec to 30s for GA and documenting cost/latency tradeoffs in the runbook.
